title: On Temporal Becoming, Relativity, and Quantum Mechanics (chapter 12)
relevance: Strongest near predecessor. Section I gives, under Stein's premises weakened by replacing transitivity with worldline cumulativity, exactly two becoming relations: R2 = 'b inside the past light cone of a' (= our J) and R1 = 'b outside the future light cone of a, or a = b' (= our B with reflexive diagonal). Registers the Clifton-Hogarth chronological weakening in footnote 3 (becoming reducible to past chronological connectibility, our I). His dichotomy premise (the spacelike region is one bloc) is the exact point where the 1+1 no-parity census splits his list. Project previously held this source only at discovery depth via Thyssen p. 41.
limits: Read from the author-posted complete web text (62.8k chars, abstract through references). The web text carries no journal pagination; printed locators below cite section boundaries only and must be re-verified against the printed chapter (pp. 229-244) before any quotation-grade use. OCR artifacts present (lost lambda/worldline glyphs, one apparently garbled clause in the transitivity counterexample prose; the definitions quoted are unaffected). Second half (quantum non-locality, Dorato 1996 critique, dynamic becoming) read at pass-through depth, not audited.
version: In Dennis Dieks (ed.), The Ontology of Spacetime II, Philosophy and Foundations of Physics vol. 4, Elsevier 2008, ch. 12, pp. 229-244, DOI 10.1016/S1871-1774(08)00012-0; author-posted web text (undated version, unpaginated)
locator: Section I: Stein's requirements (i)-(v); 'outside the future light cone' non-transitivity remark and universal transitive closure; indefiniteness relation S and its requirements; no R,S pair satisfies all clauses; exhaustiveness-drop (limbo) considered and rejected; cumulativity definition; 'two pairs of relations R1,S1 and R2,S2' definitions and transitivity verdicts; footnote 3 (CH weakening); footnote quoting CH 1995 p. 356 and Stein 1991 p. 151
assumptions: Stein's setting (Minkowski R4, time orientation): R reflexive; non-universal; causal-past inclusion (null-inclusive, both for the definite relation and for the openness relation); definability from Minkowski geometry; exhaustiveness stipulation (Rab or Sab for all a,b); full transitivity replaced by cumulativity: for every worldline and any a,b,c with b,c on the worldline, if Rab and Rbc then Rac
conclusion: Exactly two pairs (R1 = complement of the strict causal future with reflexive diagonal, = census B; R2 = closed causal past, = census J) satisfy the weakened requirements; the transitive closure of R1 is the universal relation; the elsewhere region is placed in the definite sphere (R1) or the open sphere (R2)
proof_status: Definitions, cumulativity argument and pair construction read in full; the completeness claim rests on his exhaustiveness-plus-cone-fixity dichotomy, whose quantifier structure I reconstructed; not a formally stated theorem with proof
open_questions: printed-page locators for the quoted definitions (pp. 229-244)

whether his 'future light cone' phrase means the closed causal cone (my reading, giving our B) or only the timelike interior (which would make his R1 our C); his S1 transitivity verdict and the R1/S1 exhaustiveness support the closed-causal-cone reading
whether any later work restates or criticizes the two-pair claim

title: The Definability of Objective Becoming in Minkowski Spacetime
relevance: Nearest formal predecessor with transitivity retained. Theorem 1 (pp. 365-367): definability + transitivity + reflexive chronological inclusion yields exactly I-, J-, or the universal relation. The census's transitivity row {I, J} is an immediate corollary of this theorem plus the one-line F_t exclusion of U. Their saturation proof step ('extra spacelike or future pair forces U') is the same geometric mechanism the census's no-transitivity case analysis reuses.

title: Conventionality and Reality
relevance: Prior philosophical context, upgraded this task from selective-read to primary fetch of the open-access article (47.5k chars). Section 7.1: 'The present for b ... is just the absolute elsewhere of b - a spatially extended bowtie-shaped region', invariant, partitioning M into absolute present (b + elsewhere), absolute future (upper lightcone) and absolute past (lower lightcone). Section 8.1: the transitivity objection applies to the bowtie present too. Sections 5.1 and 8.2: the reality relation R and Peterson-Silberstein's uniqueness criterion. Confirms elsewhere-only present is NOT the census's past-plus-elsewhere B or C.
limits: Primary open-access HTML fetched via exa; sections 1-2, 5.1, 7-7.2, 8.1-8.2 and conclusion read; section 3.4/3.5 (reality values, presentist credo) read at excerpt depth; conventionality-technical sections 2, 4, 6 skimmed. No census theorem or classification appears anywhere in the fetched text.
